account.note: THE POSITION WENT UNDERWATER THIS HOUR AND STILL NO EXIT IS DUE, BECAUSE BEING RED IS NOT A LEVEL EITHER. THE SIGN FLIPPED AND THE RULEBOOK DOES NOT CONTAIN THE SIGN. 46.57 at 10:22, 45.96 at 11:21, 45.77 at 12:21, 45.29 at 13:21, 44.93 now - 1.64 of bid surrendered across four hours, +3.15% to +1.79% to +1.37% to +0.31% to -0.49% on the position, and -3.27% against the 46.45 close. A position crossing its own cost is the most psychologically loaded print of the day and it is the one number in this note with NO rule attached to it: the stop is 41.54, written at entry, and the bid is 7.55% above it. Zero is not a level this book defends - if it were, every position would carry a 0% stop and no thesis would ever be given room to work. Selling here would set the stop to the entry price after the fact, which is the same defect as widening it pointed the other way. THE TIME STOP IS SESSION 5 OF 5 AND STILL FIRES AT THE CLOSE, NOT AT 14:21. The level struck at entry is the 8/14 close; the 10:21, 11:21, 12:21 and 13:21 runs each refused to contract it and this run refuses on the identical reasoning, that the day will end is true at every hour and therefore licenses selling at any of them. A red position is the strongest version yet of the argument for firing early, and it is the same argument with a worse number attached, which is exactly why it is refused again rather than re-weighed. With roughly 70 minutes to the pre-close, the practical distance between selling now and selling as written is small - and that is an argument for patience being cheap, not for the rule being optional. The pre-close owns this and the open handoff stands. Unless 54.18 or 41.54 prints first, the close sells 2 shares at the bid. THE UPST SPECIFICATION IS DEAD AND STAYS DEAD. Zero equity orders in this account for the whole session, re-checked live this hour, so the 8-share 30.59 limit never executed; UPST is 30.68 bid, 0.29% above the dead limit and -0.94% on the day. NOT re-struck and NOT graded here - its verdict belongs to the retro. NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED: the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44, this slot is exits-only with a raised bar, and the standing default is no trade. THE CANDIDATE TABLE IS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-STRUCK - its twelve rows carry the open's 09:44 bids inside a six-second window, and re-quoting only the names this run touched would publish a two-timestamp board reading as one. The exit board and the two dead watch rows carry this run's 14:21 quotes and are labelled as such. account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

entryWatch.setup: UPST breakout pullback - the reclaim held, so the reason this name was refused yesterday has half-expired and the entry is taken on the half that remains
entryWatch.trigger: EXPIRED UNFILLED AT 10:30, DEAD, AND UNCHANGED BY A FIFTH READING. The 09:44 specification - buy 8 at a 30.59 limit, target 36.71, stop 28.14, time stop the 8/20 close - reached its stated expiry without executing. The broker returns ZERO equity orders in this account for the whole session, re-checked live at 14:21, which is what confirms it: the limit is dead by an order record that is empty, not by a run's own account of itself. At 14:21 UPST is 30.68 bid / 30.71 ask, 0.29% ABOVE the dead limit and -0.94% on the day, having drifted a further 9 cents back toward it and now sitting within a dime of the price this board wanted to pay. IT IS NOT RE-STRUCK AND NOT RE-GRADED. Re-striking is refused for the reason the 10:22 run gave while the spec was still live and which expiry only strengthens: the thesis was published forced on item 1, no catalyst has appeared since, and buying the same name higher because it rose is the chase this slot's raised bar exists to refuse. That the price keeps wandering back toward the dead limit is not new information either - a limit that expired is not revived by the tape crossing it again, and treating it as revived would be re-striking on price movement alone. Grading is refused because the 8/13 board settled it across six intraday readings of one lapsed SMCI limit - +12.36, +1.38, +2.70, +0.06, +1.38, -1.38 - every verdict reversed by a later one and the final reversal flipping the sign. An intraday grade of an unexecuted specification measures the tape and not the decision. Its verdict belongs to the retro.
entryWatch.why: THE SPECIFIC REFUSAL THIS BOARD WROTE YESTERDAY NO LONGER DESCRIBES THE TAPE, AND THAT IS WHY THE NAME MOVED FROM THIRD TO FIRST. On 8/13 the open ranked UPST third and refused it on two counts: no catalyst, and 'still below BOTH structural lines the 8/6 attempt failed at - the 30.20 close it broke and the 30.32 pre-earnings level - now closing a fourth session under them'. That afternoon it closed 30.97, above both, on 4.85M shares against a 4.30M thirty-day average. The second count is spent. The first still stands and is exactly what this entry is marked forced on. A refusal whose stated reason has expired gets re-read rather than repeated. WHAT MAKES IT ITEM 2's BEST CASE RATHER THAN ITS TECHNICALITY. Yesterday was +6.4%, under the 8% the rule names, and today is -1.29% with a 30.45 session low that holds above both reclaimed lines. The rule's actual instruction is that the entry is the day-after pullback rather than the up day, and this is literally that. The rulebook lists 'breakout pullbacks' under 'Setups that fit'. WHAT IS MISSING IS THE THING THE RULEBOOK CARES ABOUT MOST. There is no catalyst - the print was 8/4, ten sessions back, and the 8/5 reaction failed outright by opening 34.595 and closing 30.20. The live calendar across 8/14 to 8/20 contains no UPST and no other watched name. So this is a chart with a level, and item 1 says in as many words that a chart is not a reason. The entry is published because the mandate requires one and this is the best available, not because the objection is answered. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME: one session above a line the name spent four sessions below is thin evidence the line has changed sides. If the 30.20/30.32 shelf gives way and the 28.14 stop is taken inside two sessions, the reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup with no catalyst had nothing holding it up.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI is refused at a price this board already refused five times yesterday, and that is the entire reason
entryWatch.trigger: STILL DEAD, NOW AT 40.12 BID / 40.13 ASK, +2.45% on the day and back within 14 cents of the 40.26 the open refused it at. The name has now round-tripped the whole intraday range this board watched it trade - 40.26 at the open, 39.28 at 12:21, 39.53 at 13:21, 40.12 now - and arrived back where it started. That is the cleanest possible demonstration of why the row is not re-argued at each new print: five readings, a full round trip, and not one of them is new information. The refusal was never about the last dollar, it was about the 27.0% the name still carries above its 31.60 pre-print close with no pullback that has held. This row is not re-argued at a lower number and is not re-argued at a higher one.
entryWatch.why: THE NUMBER DECIDES AND IT DECIDES AGAINST THE NAME THIS BOARD BOUGHT YESTERDAY. The 2026-08-10 standing tiebreak says that when a quoted number and a written thesis disagree, the number wins and the thesis is discarded. Here they do not even disagree: the thesis is the same forced item-2 failure as yesterday, and the number is worse. At 40.26 the entry is 27.4% above the 31.60 pre-print close against 25.4% when the 8/13 spec was struck, and there has still been no pullback of any kind. Reversing five documented refusals requires new information. THE ONLY NEW INFORMATION POINTS THE OTHER WAY. The 8/13 bar opened 38.28, touched 42.31 and closed 39.16 on 122.8M shares - a 7.4% fade off the high that gave back the entire day's range into the bell. A name that cannot hold its high on three times normal participation has not resolved its extension; it has demonstrated the extension. THE 8/11 PRINT IS ALSO NO LONGER THE SETUP THE RULEBOOK NAMES. 'Post-earnings day-2 continuation' is a listed setup and today is day three, with the day-2/3 pullback the rule actually prefers having never appeared. So SMCI now answers item 1 more weakly than it did yesterday while failing item 2 more badly, which is both of the directions that matter moving the wrong way at once. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT, WRITTEN AS A FIXED STATEMENT THE GRADER CAN CHECK: a pullback that holds - a defence of the 38.20 low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume - bought there rather than here. That has not appeared in three sessions and no limit was placed down there to pretend otherwise. THE DEAD 39.64 LIMIT FROM 8/13 IS RETIRED FROM THIS FILE AND ITS VERDICT BELONGS TO THE RETRO. It expired unfilled, the broker returns zero equity orders in this account, and the six intraday grades it collected yesterday - +12.36, +1.38, +2.70, +0.06, +1.38, -1.38 - are the record of why an hourly grade of a lapsed entry measures the tape rather than the decision. Re-marking it a seventh time here would be the behaviour that finding diagnoses.

entryWatch.setup: The UPST option chain misses the 10% spread ceiling by 1.7 points, which narrows the standing options finding for the third time
entryWatch.trigger: UPST 2026-09-18 calls, live chain, 35 days out: the 30 strike bid 2.41 / ask 2.71 is 11.7% of mark on 11,609 open interest and 0.590 delta. The 32.5 reads 14.3% on 0.417 delta and 1,241 open interest; the 27.5 reads 23.0% on 0.740 delta.
entryWatch.why: THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THE OPTIONS FINDING HAS BEEN NARROWED AND THE FIRST TIME IT HAS BEEN NEARLY OVERTURNED BY THE NAME THAT CREATED IT. docs/RULES.md records the original refusal as 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks', quoting UPST 9/11 calls at 25.5% of mark on 8/5. The same underlying, one chain further out, now quotes 11.7%. On 8/13 this board established that a genuinely liquid chain - SMCI at 4-6% - clears the ceiling outright, so the claim had already moved from 'options are unusable at this size' to 'the names this account could afford had unusable chains'. Today it moves again: UPST is not a liquid chain, and it is within two points of usable. The accurate statement now is that this account's universe spans 4% to 23% of mark and the ceiling cuts through the middle of it, which is a different and more useful fact than any of the three sentences that preceded it. THE CONTRACT WAS STILL NOT BOUGHT AND THE MARGIN IS NOT THE REASON. 11.7% is over 10%, the gate enforces it, and a ceiling that bends for 1.7 points is not a ceiling - that is the whole mechanism by which a rule stops existing. Two further reasons that would hold even if the spread cleared: the 30 strike at a 2.56 mark is 256.00 for one contract, and a -40% option stop puts 102.40 at risk against the 19.60 the 8-share equity risks at its stop; and the 8/13 board recorded the condition for the first option purchase as 'the next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced'. This thesis is forced. Both halves of that precedent point the same way and the spread never had to decide it.
